title: Values, types and f-strings
instructions:
## Four kinds of value

The editor defines four variables: a string, an integer, a float and a boolean. Your job is to print five lines about them using **f-strings**, which put values inside text with `{curly braces}`.

Expected output, exactly:

```
Ama is 19 years old.
Height: 1.62 m
Student: True
Next year: 20
Type of age: <class 'int'>
```

## Do this

1. Print the first three lines with one f-string each.
2. For the fourth line, do the arithmetic inside the braces: `{age + 1}`.
3. For the last line, use the built-in `type()` function inside the braces.

Then change the values at the top (a different name, age or height) and run again. The sentences should follow.

initialState.source:
name = "Ama"
age = 19
height = 1.62
is_student = True

# Print the five lines using f-strings

hints: An f-string starts with the letter f before the quote: `print(f"{name} is {age} years old.")`.
Anything inside the braces is Python: `{age + 1}` prints 20.
`type(age)` is the value `<class 'int'>`, so `print(f"Type of age: {type(age)}")`.

checks.label: The five lines come out exactly as shown
It uses f-strings
checks.message: Use f-strings (f"...") to put the values inside the text.

checks.label: It computes next year from the age variable
checks.message: Compute next year as age + 1 instead of typing 20.
